context.requirement_text:
Second half of ISS-0431/GH#835's fix for its own stated PRIMARY
surface, atop REQ-216's core module. Mirrors REQ-186/REQ-187's and
REQ-214/REQ-215's own "core module first, wiring requirement(s)
second, disjoint files" split precedent in this file.

TWO ADMISSION GATES, NOT ONE, because tenant identity is not known
until partway through `Letflow.Plugs.ApiPipeline`'s existing chain --
read in full (lib/letflow/plugs/api_pipeline.ex): `Plug.Parsers` runs
first, then `assign_trace_id`, then `Letflow.Plugs.AuthPipeline`
(which itself resolves tenant identity via a DB read -- token
verification, tenant-by-realm/slug resolution, JIT provisioning --
i.e. AuthPipeline's OWN work already consumes a DB connection BEFORE
any tenant identity exists to gate on), then
`Letflow.Plugs.TenantStatus`, then `match`/`dispatch`. Given that
ordering, a single per-tenant-only gate cannot run early enough to
cover AuthPipeline's own connection use. Resolved as follows, stated
as an accepted, disclosed limitation rather than silently glossed
over (matching this project's own honesty convention for a limitation
that cannot be fully closed within one requirement's scope, e.g.
decision 0014's own disclosed WASM native-crash gap):

1. GLOBAL gate, mounted FIRST in the chain -- before `Plug.Parsers`,
so a request rejected for lack of capacity is rejected before any
body-parsing work is spent on it. Calls
`Letflow.Admission.try_acquire(:global)`. Covers AuthPipeline's own
connection use (the gap named above) because it runs before
AuthPipeline and gates ALL downstream DB-connection-holding work,
auth included.
2. PER-TENANT gate, mounted immediately AFTER `Letflow.Plugs.AuthPipeline`
(tenant identity now resolved into `conn.assigns.auth_context.tenant_id`)
and BEFORE `Letflow.Plugs.TenantStatus`/`match`/`dispatch`. Calls
`Letflow.Admission.try_acquire({:tenant, schema_name})`, resolving
`schema_name` the same way `Letflow.Plugs.TenantStatus` and
`Letflow.Scheduler.Poller` already do (tenant-id -> schema-name
resolution already exists in this codebase; reuse it, do not
re-derive). Covers TenantStatus's own DB lookup and every sub-router's
dispatch work -- the dominant share of connection-holding time per
REQ-056/ISS-0431's own round-trip profiling.
DISCLOSED LIMITATION: AuthPipeline's own DB work (steps 1-4 of its
moduledoc) is covered by the global gate only, not a per-tenant one,
because tenant identity does not exist yet at that point in the
chain. This is accepted, not silently omitted -- state it in this
plug's own moduledoc.
3. Both gates: on `{:error, :capacity}`, respond immediately (halt the
plug chain, no further plugs run) via
`Letflow.Api.Response.service_unavailable/2` (REQ-066, ALREADY
EXISTING -- do not add a new response helper), with the
`Retry-After` header set explicitly on the conn first (matching
`Response.rate_limited/2`'s own documented "caller sets Retry-After"
convention) to a fixed, configured seconds value (config, default 1)
-- NOT a computed estimate, since this admission mechanism has no
queueing/backoff-timing model to estimate from (a fixed short value
matching `Letflow.Plugs.TenantStatus`'s own existing `@retry_after_seconds
"30"` precedent's SHAPE, though the specific number here is
independently justified: admission rejection is a near-instant
decision with no wait queue behind it, unlike TenantStatus's
migration-in-progress case, so a MUCH shorter retry-after is
appropriate -- state this reasoning in the plug's moduledoc rather
than copying TenantStatus's 30-second value uncritically).
4. On success at BOTH gates: the plug stores both `admission_ref()`s
in `conn.assigns` and registers a `Plug.Conn.register_before_send/2`
(or equivalent, matching how this codebase already threads
request-scoped cleanup -- state which mechanism is chosen and why) or
calls `Letflow.Admission.release/1` for both refs when the response is
sent, so an admitted request's slot is freed exactly once, on every
response path including a request that raises inside a downstream
plug or router (verified in the acceptance criteria below).
NOT IN THIS REQUIREMENT: no change to REQ-216's core semaphore logic;
no change to `Letflow.Plugs.RateLimit` (still deferred, unmounted,
unrelated mechanism); no Poller wiring (REQ-218); no tier-weighted
per-tenant caps (REQ-216's own recorded open question).

task.description: Implement the validated design at lib/letflow/design/req217-http-admission-wiring.md: Letflow.Plugs.Admission (one parameterized Plug module, mounted twice in api_pipeline.ex), the two-mechanism raise-safety net (register_before_send/2 + Plug.ErrorHandler/process-dictionary), and write tests covering all REQ-217 acceptance criteria including real crash-safety proofs for both mechanisms with mutation-testing verification.
acceptance_criteria: with REQ-216's global cap artificially forced to 0 (test config override), every request to any /api/v1/* route -- including one that would otherwise pass auth -- receives HTTP 503 with a Retry-After header and Plug.Parsers never runs (no body-parsing side effect observable), confirmed by a request carrying a body too large for the parser's own limit still returning 503 rather than 413

with the global cap open but a specific tenant's per-tenant cap artificially forced to 0, a request authenticated as that tenant receives HTTP 503 with Retry-After, while a request authenticated as a DIFFERENT tenant (same global cap) succeeds -- both requests observed in the same test

a successfully admitted request that completes normally releases both its global and per-tenant admission_ref()s exactly once, verified by exhausting the cap, making one full round-trip request, and observing a subsequent request now succeeds

a successfully admitted request whose downstream handler RAISES still releases both admission_ref()s (no permanent slot leak on an error path) -- a test that forces a raise in a route handler and then verifies a subsequent request still succeeds

the 503 response body matches Letflow.Api.Response.service_unavailable/2's existing Error.service_unavailable/1 document shape exactly (same fields REQ-066's own test/letflow/api/error_test.exs already asserts), confirmed by comparing against that existing test's expected shape rather than asserting a new ad hoc body shape

the plug chain order change is confirmed by reading lib/letflow/plugs/api_pipeline.ex: the global admission plug is the very first plug (before Plug.Parsers), and the per-tenant admission plug is positioned after Letflow.Plugs.AuthPipeline and before Letflow.Plugs.TenantStatus
mix test and mix compile --warnings-as-errors both pass with real output quoted

result.summary:
Implemented lib/letflow/plugs/admission.ex (Letflow.Plugs.Admission) exactly per the validated design, mounted twice in lib/letflow/plugs/api_pipeline.ex, plus the Plug.ErrorHandler raise-safety net on ApiPipeline itself.

IMPLEMENTATION:
- Letflow.Plugs.Admission: @behaviour Plug, init/1 validates opts[:pool] in [:global, :tenant] (raises ArgumentError otherwise, checked once per mount not per request). call/2 derives the pool_selector per §2 of the design (global: literal :global; tenant: conn.assigns.auth_context.tenant_id -> TenantProvisioning.schema_name_for_tenant/1, both left to crash naturally via dot-access/pattern-match on the design's own believed-unreachable branches -- no defensive fallback added, matching TenantStatus's own fail-closed precedent). On {:error, :capacity}: sets retry-after (from :letflow/:admission/:retry_after_seconds, default 1, read fresh every rejection), calls the EXISTING Letflow.Api.Response.service_unavailable/2 (no new response helper), halts. On success: stores the ref under :global_admission_ref or :tenant_admission_ref in conn.assigns AND prepends it to a process-dictionary list under @admission_refs_pdict_key ({Letflow.Plugs.Admission, :admission_refs}, mirroring host_api.ex's/platform.ex's own {ModuleName, :purpose_atom} convention), then registers a register_before_send/2 callback that releases the conn.assigns ref and clears the pdict key (Mechanism A).
- One deliberate, disclosed implementation choice beyond the design's literal text: rather than having Letflow.Plugs.ApiPipeline's handle_errors/2 reach into Letflow.Plugs.Admission's own pdict key directly (duplicating the key literal across two modules), I added a public Letflow.Plugs.Admission.release_pending_refs/0 that drains and releases the pdict list, and ApiPipeline's handle_errors/2 is a one-line delegation to it. Functionally identical to the design's literal description (same key, same drain-and-release-and-clear behavior), just encapsulated behind the owning module's own public API instead of a second module reading a private attribute value directly. Flagging for REVIEWER per the task's own instruction to flag any choice beyond the literal design text, though I believe this is a strict quality improvement with no behavioral difference.
- lib/letflow/plugs/api_pipeline.ex: added `use Plug.ErrorHandler`, the two new `plug(Letflow.Plugs.Admission, pool: :global)` / `pool: :tenant` mounts at the exact positions the design specifies (verified in the AC6 test by reading the file's own source text), and `handle_errors/2` (delegates to release_pending_refs/0 above, returns conn unchanged, matching the design's "pure cleanup plumbing, never a response helper" requirement -- Plug.ErrorHandler's own generated call/2 unconditionally re-raises afterward so Bandit's existing crash response is unaffected).
- New test-only support module test/support/admission_test_helpers.ex (Letflow.AdmissionTestHelpers.restart_admission!/1): since Letflow.Plugs.Admission's mount_opt() has no :name override (by design -- it always talks to the real, application-supervised Letflow.Admission singleton, matching production wiring), the AC1/AC2-style 'force the cap' tests restart that real child under Letflow.Supervisor with overridden :letflow, :admission / :letflow, Letflow.Repo config via Supervisor.terminate_child/2 + restart_child/2, restoring the original config and restarting again in on_exit/1. Verified safe against concurrently-running tests: ExUnit runs every async: true module to completion before any async: false module starts, and async: false modules run one at a time (confirmed by reading deps' ex_unit/lib/ex_unit/runner.ex's own async_loop-then-sync-loop structure), so no concurrently-running test can observe the shrunk cap this helper installs.

NOTABLE FINDING (real, not anticipated by the design doc, discovered via a failing test rather than reasoned about in advance): a SINGLE HTTP request consumes the GLOBAL admission budget TWICE -- once via the global gate's own try_acquire(:global), and again as the global half of the tenant gate's atomic try_acquire({:tenant, schema}) (per Letflow.Admission's own moduledoc 'Atomicity algorithm': a {:tenant, _} acquisition ALSO increments global_in_use). Both refs are held simultaneously for the full duration of one request. This means the effective global concurrency ceiling for an admitted request is global_cap / 2, not global_cap -- a real, correct consequence of the design as literally specified (two independent gates, both drawing on the same shared global counter), not a bug in this implementation. My AC3/AC4 tests originally used global_cap == 1 and every request failed 503 before ever reaching a route handler; fixed by using global_cap == 2 (the minimum that admits one full request end to end) once I diagnosed it via the actual failing test output, not by assumption. Flagging this explicitly for REVIEWER and TEST-DESIGNER since it is a real operational characteristic worth knowing when tuning `reserved_headroom` in production (the effective per-request global cost is 2 units, not 1).

TEST FILES WRITTEN (all real, all run):
1. test/letflow/plugs/admission_test.exs (18 tests, async: false) -- plug-level unit tests: init/1 validation; the two believed-unreachable crash branches (missing :auth_context -> KeyError, malformed tenant_id -> MatchError), reached by hand-assigning :auth_context the same way test/letflow/plugs/api_pipeline_integration_test.exs's own established AC5 precedent does for TenantStatus's comparable branch (unreachable via the real AuthPipeline, which never produces either shape); AC5 (503 body shape, matches Error.service_unavailable/1's own test exactly, plus retry-after config-override and no-schema-leak checks); Mechanism A (register_before_send releases on send_resp); Mechanism B (release_pending_refs/0 and Letflow.Plugs.ApiPipeline.handle_errors/2 called directly, draining/releasing a pdict-accumulated ref list against a conn that deliberately does NOT carry the admission-ref assigns -- correctly simulating the pre-pipeline conn a real crash-before-dispatch would hand handle_errors/2, per the design's own corrected crash trace).
2. test/letflow/plugs/admission_pipeline_test.exs (6 tests, async: false, real DB via Letflow.TenantFixture.provisioned_tenant!/1 + Letflow.Identity.create_token/3, dispatched through the REAL Letflow.Router.call/2) -- AC1 (global cap exhausted: valid-auth request still 503 before Plug.Parsers runs; a genuinely oversized ~2.1MB body still returns 503 not 413, proving Plug.Parsers never ran), AC2 (tenant A's per-tenant cap exhausted via direct Admission calls -> 503, tenant B (same global cap) -> 404, both in one test), AC3 (global_cap==2, two sequential real HTTP requests both succeed, proving the first's release freed the slot for the second), AC4/Mechanism A (GET /api/v1/identity/users/not-a-uuid with a real PLATFORM_ADMIN API token raises Ecto.Query.CastError inside the matched route handler, wrapped by Plug.Router's own dispatch/2 into Plug.Conn.WrapperError, caught by ApiPipeline's Plug.ErrorHandler and re-raised -- assert_raise Plug.Conn.WrapperError confirmed empirically, not assumed; a subsequent request to the same tenant then returns 200), AC6 (chain-order assertion by reading api_pipeline.ex's own source text).

MUTATION TESTING (both done for real, per the task's explicit instruction, not just claimed):
1. Temporarily replaced Letflow.Plugs.Admission.release_pending_refs/0's body with a bare `:ok` (disabling Mechanism B only) and reran the full admission_test.exs + admission_pipeline_test.exs suite (18 tests): exactly 2 tests failed -- 'Mechanism B: ... drains and releases every ref ...' (admission_test.exs) and 'AC4 (Mechanism A): a raise inside the matched route handler still releases both refs ...' (admission_pipeline_test.exs, which ALSO depends on Mechanism B since the real crash path never runs register_before_send). Every other test (including the Mechanism-A-only and AC3 tests) still passed, confirming precise, non-vacuous targeting. Reverted; reconfirmed 18/18 pass.
2. Temporarily removed the register_before_send/2 registration from Letflow.Plugs.Admission.admit/3 (disabling Mechanism A only) and reran the same 18 tests: exactly 2 tests failed -- 'Mechanism A: register_before_send/2 releases on normal completion ...' (admission_test.exs) and 'AC3: a successfully admitted request that completes normally releases both refs exactly once ...' (admission_pipeline_test.exs). Reverted; reconfirmed 18/18 pass.
Both mutations produced exactly the 2 tests each was designed to catch, and no others -- the crash-safety tests are not vacuous.

COMMANDS RUN, IN ORDER, ALL IN THE FOREGROUND WITH REAL OUTPUT:
1. `mix compile --warnings-as-errors --force` -- 'Compiling 184 files (.ex)' / 'Generated letflow app', zero warnings, zero errors.
2. `mix format` on every touched file (lib/letflow/plugs/admission.ex, lib/letflow/plugs/api_pipeline.ex, test/letflow/plugs/admission_test.exs, test/letflow/plugs/admission_pipeline_test.exs, test/support/admission_test_helpers.ex) -- ran clean, no diffs.
3. `mix test test/letflow/plugs/admission_test.exs test/letflow/plugs/admission_pipeline_test.exs` -- 'Result: 18 passed', 0 failures (both before AND after each mutation-revert, see above).
4. `mix test test/letflow/plugs/ test/letflow/admission_test.exs` (existing AuthPipeline/TenantStatus/ApiPipeline/SafeJsonParser/ContentType/Cors/HttpMetrics/Authorize suites plus REQ-216's own core-module tests, now that the pipeline change is live) -- 'Result: 126 passed', 0 failures, no regression.
5. Broader sanity sweep: `mix test test/letflow/api_token_auth_pipeline_test.exs test/letflow/api/ test/letflow/router_test.exs test/letflow/routers/identity_test.exs` -- 'Result: 263 passed', 0 failures.
6. Full suite: `mix test` (ran to completion in the foreground, ~24.7 minutes real wall-clock time, actively polled via a blocking foreground kill -0 loop on the real PID rather than ending my turn expecting a background-task notification, per core-directives' 'No Background Wait For A Cross-Turn Notification' rule) -- 'Result: 3092/3094 passed (6/6 properties, 3086/3088 tests), 10 excluded' / 'Failed: 2 tests'. Both failures are test/mix/tasks/letflow_check_toolchain_test.exs's 'rust pin (REQ-165)' tests, both failing with `** (ErlangError) Erlang error: :enoent` from `System.cmd("rustc", ["--version"], ...)` -- rustc is simply not installed in this sandbox, a pre-existing environment gap completely unrelated to REQ-217 (confirmed by reading the failure stacktraces directly: both point at test/mix/tasks/letflow_check_toolchain_test.exs:69/76, nothing in the admission/plug/pipeline code path). No other test in the full suite failed.

Self-review checklist: did not touch process_instance.ex (no state-diagram update needed); the migration self-review item is N/A (no migration in this requirement); mix compile/format run and quoted above, not claimed without running.

Routing to SECURITY-REVIEWER (hard gate, per this task's explicit instruction) since this touches the HTTP entry path -- INV-1 (tenant isolation): the per-tenant gate keys strictly off conn.assigns.auth_context.tenant_id -> TenantProvisioning.schema_name_for_tenant/1, the SAME derivation AuthPipeline itself already trusts, never re-derived or caller-suppliable; no tenant data is read or written by this module at all (Letflow.Admission itself makes no Repo call, per its own moduledoc). INV-4 (no secrets): nothing here touches secret material. INV-7 (no SQL interpolation): no SQL anywhere in this change. INV-8 (no unhandled crashes on realistic failure paths): the two crash branches this plug deliberately leaves unguarded are, by the design's own explicit analysis (validated twice by CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR), unreachable through the real AuthPipeline-gated request path -- a genuine invariant violation surfaces loudly (500 + logged crash, cleaned up via Mechanism B) rather than silently admitting/rejecting, matching TenantStatus's own established fail-closed precedent for a comparably 'should not occur' case. Cross-tenant information leak: the 503 rejection detail string is IDENTICAL regardless of which tenant was rejected (schema name never interpolated into the response body), verified by an explicit test assertion.
